Action Plan:
1. Schedule urgent in-person appointment with clinic support team for full neurological examination, fundoscopy, and blood pressure measurement.  
2. Prescribe a stronger NSAID (name/dose/route/frequency not documented) to be taken with food; patient may take paracetamol concomitantly.  
3. Continue current combined oral contraceptive pill; reassess pill suitability after examination—change may be required if migraine with visual aura confirmed.  
4. Provide red-flag safety-netting: if headache becomes unbearable, changes in character, or new neurological symptoms develop, attend Emergency Department or call clinic immediately.  
5. Patient to monitor symptoms; if headache fully resolves before scheduled review, appointment can be cancelled.  
6. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Reason for visit: “blinding” headache for 3 days; unable to work effectively.  
• History of presenting complaint  
  – Onset: sudden, on waking, 3 days ago.  
  – Location: generalized, worse over right eye.  
  – Character: constant; severity 8/10, decreases to ~5/10 with ibuprofen.  
  – Associated symptoms: photophobia, occasional “shooting lights” in vision, mild nausea (no vomiting). No focal neurological deficits, no fever, no sinus/respiratory symptoms, no positional cough-related exacerbation; mild stabbing pain when standing quickly or sudden head movement.  
  – Course: persistent; not waking her at night but present on waking. Ibuprofen provides partial temporary relief.  
• Past medical history: childhood abdominal pain (resolved, no diagnosis).  
• Family history: mother suffers from migraines with vomiting.  
• Medications:  
  – Combined oral contraceptive pill (brand/dose not documented) – started 1 year ago.  
  – Ibuprofen as needed for headache.  
• Allergies: none known.  
• Social history: lives alone; non-smoker; drinks alcohol “about three” drinks once weekly; no recreational drugs.

Objective:
• No physical examination performed during telehealth consult.  
• No vitals or investigations available.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute severe headache
   - Likely diagnosis: Migraine (possible migraine with visual aura).  
   - Differential: Tension-type headache, sinus headache, medication-overuse headache, secondary causes (e.g., intracranial pathology) – to be ruled out by examination.  
   - Investigations planned: In-person neurological exam, fundoscopy, blood pressure measurement; further imaging/labs if indicated after assessment.  
   - Treatment planned: Prescribe stronger NSAID (details not documented) plus optional paracetamol; advise taking with food. Provide safety-netting and ED advice if deterioration.

2. Combined oral contraceptive pill suitability
   - Assessment: Current COC may be contraindicated if migraine with aura confirmed.  
   - Plan: Review BP at face-to-face visit; consider switching to non-estrogen method if migraine with aura diagnosed.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: vitals, in-person neurological/ophthalmic exam, exact medication names/doses, detailed migraine history, menstrual history, last eye test report.  
● No internal conflicts noted.  
● Transcript quality: generally clear; brief audio dropouts but clinical content decipherable.
